correctness.rationale: Fix terminal bits; all internal degree-two vertices are valid exactly when their path word avoids \(101\). The two terminal degree-r vertices impose at most one chosen first/last internal bit when absent. Filtering the product of four-state path factors yields an exhaustive bijection. For path length three, the four terminal cases contribute \((1+rz)^2\), twice \(z((1+z)^r+rz^2(1+z)^{r-1})\), and \(z^2(1+z^2)^r\); these are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. Positive coefficients give exact support and r maximal proper sets. The accompanying verifier independently checks original adjacency constraints and transfer coefficients on six equal-length and twelve mixed-length instances; no finite check is misused as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The newly studied \(P_3\)-convex-set counting problem is nontrivial on cyclic graph classes. Generalized theta graphs form a canonical non-tree series-parallel family: all arms couple at two high-degree terminals, so naively multiplying path counts is wrong. The exact full-size polynomial and its noninterval cardinality support explain a structural obstruction—whole ranges of odd sizes are forbidden—while the \(r\) largest proper sets have a rigid explicit form. This extends the motivated enumeration program beyond the published tree/threshold formulas, rather than tabulating an arbitrary small graph.
